subject: MedicoHealth: urgent regional evacuation & stabilization request
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medicohealth.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: NetworkOps <ops@medicohealth.com>, Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@medicohealth.com>
Date: 2025-04-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected latency + 5xx in us-west-2 (AZ2) — immediate help needed

Rafael,

We're seeing a sharp spike in 5xx and end-to-end latency starting ~09:00 PDT in us-west-2 (AZ2). Checkout failures for about ~12% of sessions and a sustained token-latency increase (p50 -> 340ms, p95 -> 1.8s). This is happening for our production tenant (MedicoHealth prod) and is impacting transactions.

Attached is a log bundle and a couple of curl traces — the errors look like repeated 502s coming from the inference tier. Our NetworkOps has already checked networking and there are no cloud-level alerts on our side. Can Redwood evict AZ2 traffic and route to a healthy region (us-west-1 or us-east-1) and/or flip us to the standby model variant? We need an authorization to failover or a recommendation for an immediate mitigation.

Attachments: medico-logs-20250422.zip (log bundle), diagnostic-screenshot.png

--
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Ops, MedicoHealth
liam.oconnor@medicohealth.com
+1 415-555-0124

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medicohealth.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2025-04-22T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency + 5xx in us-west-2 (AZ2) — immediate help needed

Liam — thanks for the heads up and the logs. Looping in Hannah (SRE lead), Grace (Customer Success) and Steph (sales/credits lead).

Immediate plan (we're initiating now):
- Hannah: please execute the geo-evacuation play (redirect 100% of MedicoHealth prod traffic from us-west-2 -> us-west-1) and enable the model-variant fallback for any incompatible endpoints.
- We'll enable prefix/KV warm-up to reduce cold-KV misses during the shift.
- Set short token-level throttles for heavy background jobs to protect tail latency.

Grace: please keep MedicoOps informed and confirm the window for accepting routed traffic.
Steph: we'll likely need to offer a temporary SLA credit for the outage window; please prepare recommended credit amounts once we have stabilization time.

Hannah — can you confirm ETA to stable traffic (ballpark)? I will send an exec note shortly once we have stabilization.

-Rafael
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medicohealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2025-04-22T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency + 5xx in us-west-2 (AZ2) — immediate help needed

On Tue, Apr 22, 2025 at 09:35 AM rafael_mendes@redwood.com wrote:
> Hannah: please execute the geo-evacuation play (redirect 100% of MedicoHealth prod traffic from us-west-2 -> us-west-1) and enable the model-variant fallback for any incompatible endpoints.

Action log / status: 
- Started evacuation at 09:43 PDT. Initiated weighted steering -> us-west-1.
- KV-cache warm-up in flight (preheating most-used prefixes). Expect ~60s for hit-rate to climb.
- Model-variant fallback activated for routes that report incompatible quant configs.
- Traffic now at ~85% routed to us-west-1, 15% still hitting us-west-2 as edge drains. Error rate dropping (5xx from ~12% -> 2.3%). Latency p95 trending down toward 700ms.

Estimated stabilization: 3-7 minutes after full drain completes (dependent on KV warm-up and active sessions). I'll keep rolling updates here.

Attachments: evac-playbook-20250422.pdf (playbook excerpt)

--
Hannah Schmitt
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medicohealth.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2025-04-22T10:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency + 5xx in us-west-2 (AZ2) — immediate help needed

Thanks Hannah, Rafael — we see traffic shifting and latency improving on our end. 5xx dropped to ~1.5% and checkout errors are back under the threshold. Appreciate the quick response.

Two quick asks:
1) How long do you expect the cross-region steering to stay in place? We need to know to adjust our routing and CDN TTLs.
2) We'll still need a short incident summary for our compliance/audit record and confirmation of the exact affected window (start/end times) for invoicing/credits.

If traffic continues to stabilize we'll stand down our mitigations. Please advise on next steps and any customer-facing comms.

--
Liam

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2025-04-22T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: MedicoHealth — incident summary & exec ask (post-stabilization)

Team — closing notes for the incident earlier today (finalizing for MedicoHealth):
- Affected window: 2025-04-22T09:00:00-07:00 to 2025-04-22T10:12:00-07:00 (root cause investigation still in progress; preliminary signal indicates an AZ-localized inference node preemption cascade causing kernel-level degradation).
- Mitigation: Geo-evacuation (us-west-2 -> us-west-1), model-variant fallback, KV warm-up, and short throttles for heavy background jobs. Traffic fully normal by ~10:12 PDT.
- Customer impact: elevated latency and ~12% 5xx at peak; MedicoHealth reported checkout failures for a subset of sessions.
- Action items: Hannah to file INF ticket with kernel trace attach and remediation steps (INF-3124). Grace to prepare a customer-facing incident brief. Steph to prepare a proposed SLA credit (recommended 10% of monthly usage for the 72-minute window) and coordinate approvals with finance.

Requests for execs: please approve the recommended credit hold (Steph's proposal) and sign-off on the customer note prior to sending. I'll attach the incident brief once Grace completes it.

Thanks everyone for the quick coordination.

-Rafael
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
